Khaiser Begum vs The State Of Telangana And 2 Others on 1
November, 2022
Bench: A.Abhishek Reddy, Juvvadi Sridevi
 The Hon'Ble Sri Justice A.Abhishek Reddy

 The Hon'Ble Smt Justice Juvvadi Sridevi

Order:

entities.text: Khaiser Begum vs The State Of Telangana And 2 Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
{Per the Hon'ble Sri Justice A.Abhishek Reddy} Smt Khaiser Begum, the wife of the detenu, has filed the present Writ Petition, challenging the detention order vide SB (I) No.60/PD-3/HYD/2022,
dated 25.02.2022 passed by the respondent No.2-Commissioner of Police & Additional District Magistrate (Executive), Hyderabad, whereby, the alleged detenu was detained under Section 3 (2) of the Telangana Prevention of Dangerous Activities of Bootleggers, Dacoits, Drug-Offenders,
Goondas, Immoral Traffic Offenders, Land-Grabbers, Spurious Seed Offenders, Insecticide Offenders, Fertiliser Offenders, Food Adulteration Offenders, Fake Document Offenders, Scheduled Commodities Offenders, Forest Offenders, Gaming Offenders, Sexual Offenders, Explosive Substances Offenders, Arms Offenders, Cyber Crime Offenders and White Collar or Financial Offenders Act, 1986 (for short, 'the PD Act'), and the consequential confirmation order vide G.O.Rt.No.1074, General AAR,J & JS,J Administration (Spl. Law & Order) Department, dated 21.05.2022, passed by the Secretary to Government, General Administration (Spl. Law & Order)
Department, Government of Telangana.

entities.text: Commissioner of Police & Additional District Magistrate (Executive), Hyderabad
entities.label: RESPONDENT

entities.text: Telangana Prevention of Dangerous Activities of Bootleggers, Dacoits
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text:
2. Heard the learned counsel for petitioner and learned Special Government Pleader appearing on behalf of the learned Additional Advocate General for the respondents and perused the record.
3.

The case of the petitioner is that basing on five (5) crimes viz., Crime No.112 of 2021 of Chatrinaka Police Station, Crime No.164 of 2021 of Falaknuma Police Station, and Crime Nos.286, 338 and 360 of 2021 of Chandrayangutta Police Station, the respondent No.2 passed the impugned detention order, dated 25.02.2022.
According to the respondent No.2, the alleged detenu is a 'Goonda', as, he has been habitually committing burglaries in the limits of Hyderabad Police Commissionerate.
He has been causing large scale fear and panic among the general public, thus adversely affecting the public order, peace and tranquility in the area.
Subsequently, the impugned detention order was confirmed by the Government vide G.O.Rt.No.1074, dated 21.05.2022.
AAR,J & JS,J 4.
Learned counsel for the petitioner would contend that the impugned detention order has been passed in a mechanical manner and without application of mind.
Already criminal law was set into motion against the detenu.

The impugned detention order was passed on the mere apprehension Khaiser Begum vs The State Of Telangana And 2 Others on 1 November, 2022 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/12992713/
1

entities.text: Khaiser Begum vs The State Of Telangana And 2 Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: that the detenu has admitted his guilt in four cases to get away with simple imprisonment and there is every possibility of his admitting guilt in the remaining cases also for securing simple conviction and that after releasing from prison, there is imminent possibility of the detenu indulging in similar prejudicial activities again, which is unjustified.
The alleged crimes do not add up to "disturbing the public order" and they are confined within the ambit and scope of the words "law and order".
Since the offences alleged are under the Indian Penal Code, the detenu can certainly be tried and convicted thereunder.
Thus, there is no need for the detaining authority to invoke the draconian preventive detention law against the detenu.
Hence, the impugned orders tantamount to colourable exercise of power.

The impugned orders are legally unsustainable and ultimately, prayed to allow the Writ Petition, as prayed for.
AAR,J & JS,J 5.

On the other hand, the learned Special Government Pleader appearing for the respondents supported the impugned orders and submitted that the alleged detenu is a 'Goonda' and has been habitually committing burglaries in the limits of Hyderabad Police Commissionerate and thereby acting in a manner prejudicial to the maintenance of public order.
Therefore, the apprehension of the detaining authority that there is every likelihood of the detenu committing similar offences is not misconceived.
The series of crimes allegedly committed by the detenu were sufficient to cause a feeling of insecurity in the minds of the people at large.
Therefore, the detaining authority is legally justified in passing the impugned detention order.
Subsequently, vide G.O.Rt.No.1074, dated 21.05.2022, the Government confirmed the impugned detention order.
All the mandatory requirements were strictly followed by the detaining authority while passing the impugned detention order.
The impugned orders are legally sustainable and ultimately, prayed to dismiss the Writ Petition.

6. In view of the submissions made by both the sides, the point that arises for determination in this Writ Petition is:
A A R , J & J S , J " W h e t h e r t h e i m p u g n e d d e t e n t i o n o r d e r v i d e S B ( I )
No.60/PD-3/HYD/2022, dated 25.02.2022 passed by the respondent No.2, and the consequential confirmation order vide G.O.Rt.No.1074, General Administration (Spl.
Law & Order) Department, dated 21.05.2022 passed by the respondent No.1, are liable to be set aside?"

POINT:
7.
In catena of cases, the Hon'ble Supreme Court had clearly opined that there is a vast difference between "law and order" and "public order".

The offences committed against a particular individual fall within the ambit of "law and order" and when the public at large is adversely affected by the criminal activities of a person, such activities of that person are said to disturb the public order.
Moreover, individual cases can be dealt with by the criminal justice system.
Therefore, there is no need for the detaining authority to invoke the draconian preventive detention laws against an individual.

Hence, according to the Hon'ble Apex Court, the detaining authority should be wary of Khaiser Begum vs The State Of Telangana And 2 Others on 1 November, 2022 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/12992713/
2 invoking the immense power under the Act.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: AAR,J & JS,J 8.
In Ram Manohar Lohia v. State of Bihar1, the Hon'ble Supreme Court has, in fact, deprecated the invoking of the preventive law in order to tackle a law and order problem.

entities.text: Ram Manohar Lohia v. State of Bihar1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It was observed that every breach of public peace and every violation of law may create a 'law and order' problem, but does not necessarily create a problem of 'public order'.
The distinction has to be borne in mind in view of what has been stated in the grounds of detention.

9. In Kanu Biswas v. State of West Bengal2, the Hon'ble Apex Court, while discussing the meaning of word 'public order,' held that the question whether a man has only committed a breach of 'law and order' or has acted in a manner likely to cause a disturbance of the 'public order', is a question of degree and extent of the reach of the act upon the Society.

entities.text: Kanu Biswas v. State of West Bengal2
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 10. In the present case, the detaining authority, basing on five (5) crimes indicated above, has passed the impugned detention order dated 25.02.2022.

We shall present them in a tabular form,
the date of occurrence, the date of registration of FIR, the offence AIR 1966 SC 740 (1972) 3 SCC 831 AAR,J & JS,J complained of and its nature, such as bailable/non-bailable or cognizable/non-cognizable.

Chandrayanagutta 11.08.2021 11.08.2021 and 380 of Non  PS IPC Bailable Khaiser Begum vs The State Of Telangana And 2 Others on 1 November, 2022 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/12992713/
3 11.
As seen from the material placed on record, the five (5) crimes relied on by the detaining authority for preventively detaining the detenu relate to committing burglaries.

Further, out of five cases, the detenu admitted his guilt in four cases and was convicted and sentenced to undergo simple imprisonment for four AAR,J & JS,J months with a fine of Rs.200/- and the other case is pending trial.
Thus, as on the date of passing of the impugned detention order, the detenu continues to be in judicial custody.

Under these circumstances, the apprehension of the detaining authority that there is every likelihood of the detenu indulging in similar offences, which are prejudicial to the maintenance of public order, unless he is prevented from doing so by an order of detention, is highly misplaced.
It is the bounden duty of the Police to inform the learned Public Prosecutor about the conduct of the detenu and to hand over the entire case record available in respect of the alleged detenu.

The police are supposed to be vigilant in collecting the whole data against the detenu and furnish the same to the Public Prosecutor/Additional Public Prosecutor to defeat the bail application/s of the alleged detenu.
Moreover, criminal law was already set into motion against the alleged detenu.

Further, since the alleged detenu has allegedly committed offence punishable under the Indian Penal Code, the said crime can be effectively dealt with under the provisions of the Penal Code and there was no need for the detaining authority to invoke the draconian preventive detention law.

Thus, the offences allegedly committed by the AAR,J & JS,J alleged detenu in the five (5) crimes, relied on by the detaining authority, do not fall within the ambit of the words "public order"
or "disturbance of public order".
Instead, they fall within the scope of the words "law and order".
Hence, there was no need for the detaining authority to pass the impugned detention order.

The detaining authority cannot be permitted to subvert,
supplant or substitute the punitive law of land, by ready resort to preventive detention.
12. For the foregoing reasons, the impugned orders are legally unsustainable and are liable to be set aside.
13. In the result, the Writ Petition is allowed.

The impugned detention order vide SB (I)
No.60/PD-3/HYD/2022, dated 25.02.2022 passed by the respondent No.2 and the consequential confirmation order vide G.O.Rt.No.1074, General Administration (Spl. Law & Order) Department,
dated 21.05.2022, are hereby set aside.

The respondents are directed to set the alleged detenu,
namely, Mohammed Saleem @ Sunil Shetty @ Ibrahim @ Setty Saleem, S/o late Mohammed Jahangir at liberty forthwith, in case he is no longer required in any other criminal case.
AAR,J & JS,J
